              <td align="left" valign="top" width="95%">
                <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -49.7pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Business</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Historical</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Dialysis Corporation of America, a
Florida corporation organized in 1976, develops, owns, and operates outpatient
kidney dialysis centers that provide quality dialysis and ancillary services to
patients suffering from chronic kidney failure, generally referred to as end
stage renal disease, or ESRD.&#160;&#160;We also provide acute inpatient
dialysis treatments in hospitals, homecare services and dialysis center
management services.&#160;&#160;We currently own 37 outpatient dialysis
facilities.&#160;&#160;During 2008 we acquired the assets of two dialysis
facilities located in Georgia and Maryland, the Georgia facility having
previously been managed by us, and we opened a new facility in
Pennsylvania.&#160;&#160;We also engage, on a limited basis, in medical product
sales.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our principal executive offices are
located at 1302 Concourse Drive, Suite 204, Linthicum, Maryland 21090, and you
may contact us as follows:</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 72pt"></font>Telephone: (410) 694-0500</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 72pt"></font>Fax: (410) 694-0596</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 72pt"></font>Email:
info@dialysiscorporation.com</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our internet website can be found at
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">www.dialysiscorporation.com</font>.&#160;&#160;You
may obtain through our internet website, free of charge, our annual report on
Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K,
amendments to those reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission,
referred to as the SEC, press releases, corporate profiles and corporate
governance materials.&#160;&#160;We also make those documents available to
shareholders free of charge upon request.&#160;&#160;The SEC maintains a website
at <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">www.sec.gov</font>
where our reports and other information about us may be obtained</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our company distinguishes itself on the
basis of quality patient care delivered by patient-focused, courteous, highly
trained professional staff.&#160;&#160;In addition to outpatient facilities, we
provide acute inpatient dialysis treatments that are conducted under contractual
relationships with hospitals located in near proximity to certain of our
outpatient facilities.&#160;&#160;Currently we have 11 such
relationships.&#160;&#160;Our homecare services, primarily through the use of
peritoneal dialysis, requires us to provide equipment and supplies, training,
monitoring and follow-up assistance to patients who are able to perform their
treatments at home.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our medical services revenue is derived
primarily from four sources: (i) outpatient hemodialysis services (ii) home and
peritoneal dialysis services; (iii) inpatient hemodialysis services for acute
patient care provided through agreements with hospitals and medical centers; and
(iv) ancillary services associated with dialysis treatments, including the
administration of erythropoietin (&#8220;EPO&#8221;), a bio-engineered protein that
stimulates the production of red blood cells (a deteriorating kidney loses its
ability to regulate red blood cell count, resulting in
anemia).&#160;&#160;Dialysis is an ongoing and necessary therapy to sustain life
for ESRD patients.&#160;&#160;ESRD patients typically receive up to 156 dialysis
treatments each year.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Essential to our operations and income
is Medicare reimbursement which is a fixed rate determined by the Center for
Medicare and Medicaid Services (&#8220;CMS&#8221;) of the Department of Health and Human
Services (&#8220;HHS&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The level of our revenues and profitability may be
adversely affected by future legislation that could result in rate
cuts.&#160;&#160;Further, our operating costs tend to increase over the years in
excess of increases in the prescribed dialysis treatment
rates.&#160;&#160;Congress approved a 1.6% composite rate increase for each of
2005 and 2006, and a 1.6% increase that was effective April 1,
2007.&#160;&#160;Also for 2007, the drug add-on adjustment to the composite rate
increased 0.5%.&#160;&#160;In 2005, Medicare implemented an additional change in
the manner it reimburses dialysis treatments, which includes a pricing revision
to the current average wholesale price for separately billable drugs and
biologicals.&#160;&#160;Effective January 1, 2006, payments for pharmaceuticals
(including EPO) were set at the pharmaceutical&#8217;s average sales price as
determined by the Inspector General of HHS, plus 6%, which remained the same for
2007 and 2008.&#160;&#160;Effective April, 2006, CMS implemented a policy for
monitoring the dosage of EPO based upon the patient&#8217;s hematocrit level and for
limiting the quantity of EPO that can be administered in any one
month.&#160;&#160;Effective January 1, 2008, CMS further decreased the quantity
of EPO that may be administered in any month.&#160;&#160;Medicare has
implemented a case mix payment system, adjusting the composite rate for a
limited number of patient characteristics.&#160;&#160;The increase in the
composite rate is intended to offset reductions in pharmaceutical
reimbursements.&#160;&#160;In July, 2008, Congress passed legislation aimed at
establishing a broader &#8220;bundling&#8221; reimbursement system which is intended to take
effect incrementally beginning in 2011.&#160;&#160;See under this Item 1,
&#8220;Operations &#8211; Medicare Reimbursement.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Commercial third-party
reimbursement rates, which have increased as a percentage of our revenues over
the last two years, are also susceptible to reduction.&#160;&#160;The inpatient
dialysis service agreements for treating acute kidney disease are not subject to
government fixed rates, but rather are negotiated with
hospitals.&#160;&#160;Typically these rates are higher than the government fixed
rates on a per treatment basis.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Dialysis
Industry</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Kidneys act as filters removing harmful
substances and excess water from the blood, enabling the body to maintain proper
and healthy balances of chemicals and water.&#160;&#160;Chronic kidney failure,
or ESRD, results from chemical imbalance and buildup of toxic chemicals, and is
a state of kidney disease characterized by advanced irreversible renal
impairment.&#160;&#160;ESRD is a likely consequence of complications resulting
from diabetes, hypertension, advanced age, and specific hereditary, cystic and
urological diseases.&#160;&#160;ESRD patients, in order to survive, must either
obtain a kidney transplant, which procedure is limited due to lack of suitable
kidney donors and the incidence of rejection of transplanted organs, or obtain
dialysis treatments for the rest of their lives.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Based upon CMS information published in
the 2008 United States Renal Data System, the number of ESRD patients requiring
dialysis treatments in the United States in 2006 exceeded 350,000, with a growth
rate of approximately 3% to 4% a year.&#160;&#160;This is thought to be
attributable primarily to the </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">aging of
the population, greater patient longevity as a result of improved dialysis
technology, and better treatment and survival rates for illnesses that lead to
chronic kidney disease.&#160;&#160;The statistics further reflect over 5,067
dialysis facilities, with a current annual cost for treating ESRD patients in
the United States of approximately $31 billion in 2006, of which Medicare
accounted for approximately $23 billion.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>ESRD Treatment Options</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Treatment options for ESRD patients
include: (1) hemodialysis, performed either at (i) an outpatient facility, (ii)
inpatient hospital facility, or (iii) the patient&#8217;s home; (2) peritoneal
dialysis, either continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis or continuous cycling
peritoneal dialysis; or (3) kidney transplant.&#160;&#160;A significant portion
of ESRD patients receive treatments at non-hospital owned outpatient dialysis
facilities (according to CMS, approximately 82%) with most of the remaining
patients treated at home through hemodialysis or peritoneal
dialysis.&#160;&#160;Patients treated at home are monitored by a designated
outpatient facility.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The most prevalent form of treatment
for ESRD patients is hemodialysis, which involves the use of an artificial
kidney, known as a dialyzer, to perform the function of removing toxins and
excess fluids from the bloodstream.&#160;&#160;This is accomplished with a
dialysis machine, a complex blood filtering device which takes the place of
certain functions of the kidney, and also controls external blood flow and
monitors the toxic and fluid removal process.&#160;&#160;The dialyzer has two
separate chambers divided by a semi-permeable
membrane.&#160;&#160;Simultaneously with the blood circulating through one
chamber, dialyzer fluid is circulated through the other chamber.&#160;&#160;The
toxins and excess fluid pass through the membrane into the dialysis
fluid.&#160;&#160;On the average, patients usually receive three treatments per
week with each treatment taking three to five hours.&#160;&#160;Dialysis
treatments are performed by teams of licensed nurses and trained technicians
pursuant to the physician&#8217;s instructions.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Home hemodialysis treatment requires
the patient to be medically suitable and have a qualified
assistant.&#160;&#160;Additionally, home hemodialysis requires training for both
the patient and the patient&#8217;s assistant, which usually encompasses four to eight
weeks.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>A second home treatment option for ESRD
patients is peritoneal dialysis.&#160;&#160;The two most common forms of
peritoneal dialysis are continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis and continuous
cycling peritoneal dialysis.&#160;&#160;All forms of peritoneal dialysis use the
patient&#8217;s peritoneal (abdominal) cavity to eliminate fluid and toxins from the
patient.&#160;&#160;Continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis utilizes dialysis
solution infused manually into the patient&#8217;s peritoneal cavity through a
surgically-placed catheter.&#160;&#160;The solution is allowed to remain in the
abdominal cavity for a three to five hour period and is then
drained.&#160;&#160;The process is then repeated.&#160;&#160;Continuous cycling
peritoneal dialysis is performed in a manner similar to continuous ambulatory
peritoneal dialysis, but utilizes a mechanical device to cycle the dialysis
solution while the patient is sleeping.&#160;&#160;Peritoneal dialysis is the
third most common form of ESRD therapy following center hemodialysis and renal
transplant.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>While kidney transplantation is
typically the most desirable form of therapeutic intervention, the scarcity of
suitable donors and possibility of donee rejection limits the availability of
this surgical procedure as a treatment option.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Business
Strategy</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Dialysis Corporation of America has 33
years&#8217; experience in developing and operating dialysis treatment
facilities.&#160;&#160;Our priority is to provide quality patient
care.&#160;&#160;We continue to establish alliances with physicians and
hospitals and attempt to initiate dialysis service arrangements with nursing
homes and managed care organizations.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We actively seek and negotiate with
physicians and others to establish new outpatient dialysis
facilities.&#160;&#160;In 2008, we acquired two centers and opened one new
center.&#160;&#160;We are in different phases of negotiations with physicians
for potential new facilities in a variety of states.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Same
Center Growth</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We endeavor to increase same center
growth by adding quality staff and management and attracting new patients to our
existing facilities.&#160;&#160;We seek to accomplish this objective by
rendering high caliber patient care in convenient, safe and pleasant
conditions.&#160;&#160;We believe that we have adequate space and stations
within our facilities to accommodate greater patient volume and maximize our
treatment potential.&#160;&#160;Same center growth relates to those centers that
were operable during the entire prior year.&#160;&#160;During 2008, we
experienced approximately 5% increase in dialysis treatments for our facilities
that qualified to be included in same center growth compared to 6% during the
preceding year.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Development
and Acquisition of Facilities</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>One of the primary elements in
developing or acquiring facilities is locating an area with an existing patient
base under the current treatment of local nephrologists interested in working
with a dialysis center, since the proposed facility would primarily be serving
such patients.&#160;&#160;Other considerations in evaluating development of a
dialysis facility or a proposed acquisition are the types of commercial
insurance in the area and the ESRD patient census they serve, availability and
cost of qualified and skilled personnel, particularly nursing and technical
staff, the size and condition of the facility and its equipment, the atmosphere
for the patients, the area&#8217;s demographics and population growth estimates, state
regulation of dialysis and healthcare services, and the existence of competitive
factors such as existing outpatient dialysis facilities within reasonable
proximity to the proposed center.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Expansion is either through the
development of new dialysis facilities, or acquisition of existing outpatient
dialysis centers.&#160;&#160;While acquisition of existing outpatient dialysis
centers is a faster means for achieving profitability, these transactions can be
more costly, and therefore, the company takes a selective approach to its
acquisition strategy.&#160;&#160;The primary reason for physicians selling or
participating in the development of centers is the avoidance of administrative
and financial responsibilities, freeing their time to devote to their
professional practice.&#160;&#160;Other motivating forces are the physician&#8217;s
desire to be part of a larger organization allowing for economies of scale and
the ability to realize a return on their investment if they have an interest in
the dialysis entity.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>To construct and develop a new facility
ready for operation takes an average of four to six months, and usually up to 12
months or longer to generate earnings, all of which are subject to variables
based on location, size and competitive elements.&#160;&#160;Some of our centers
are in the developmental stage, since they have not reached the point where the
patient base is sufficient to generate and sustain earnings.&#160;&#160;See Item
7, &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of
Operations.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Construction of a 15 station facility, typically the
size of our dialysis facilities, costs in a range of $1,000,000 to $1,500,000,
including equipment and initial working capital requirements, and is dependent
upon location, size and related services to be provided by the proposed
facility.&#160;&#160;An acquisition of an existing facility is usually based
primarily upon the patient base and earnings, and to a lesser extent, location
and competition.&#160;&#160;As a result, the costs associated with an
acquisition of a facility can be substantially greater than that of a
development; therefore, we selectively identify potential
acquisitions.&#160;&#160;Any significant expansion, whether through acquisition
or development of new facilities, is dependent upon existing funds or financing
from other sources.&#160;&#160;We have a revolving credit facility intended to
provide available funds for the development and acquisition of new dialysis
facilities and for other</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">general

Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of
Operations.&#8221;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Inpatient
Services</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We also provide acute dialysis
treatments through contracts with hospitals for inpatient dialysis
services.&#160;&#160;These contracts are primarily sought with hospitals in
areas serviced by our facilities.&#160;&#160;Hospitals are willing to enter into
such inpatient care arrangements to eliminate the administrative burdens of
providing dialysis services to their patients as well as the expense involved in
maintaining dialysis equipment, supplies and personnel.&#160;&#160;We believe
that these arrangements are beneficial to our operations, since the contract
rates are individually negotiated with each hospital and are not fixed by
government regulation as is the case with Medicare reimbursement fees for ESRD
patient treatment.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There is
no certainty as to when any additional centers or service contracts will be
implemented, or, to the extent implemented, the number of dialysis stations or
patient treatments these centers or service contracts may involve, or if they
will ultimately be profitable.&#160;&#160;There is no assurance that we will be
able to continue to enter into favorable relationships with physicians who would
become medical directors of proposed dialysis facilities, or that we will be
able to acquire or develop any new dialysis centers within a favorable
geographic area.&#160;&#160;Newly established dialysis centers, although
contributing to increased revenues, also adversely affect results of operations
due to their start-up costs and expenses and to their having a smaller and
slower developing patient base.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Business Strategy,&#8221; &#8220;Operations&#8221;
and &#8220;Competition&#8221; of this Item 1, and Item 7, &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and
Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.&#8221;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Operations</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Location, Capacity and Use of
Facilities</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We currently own 37 outpatient dialysis
facilities in Georgia, Maryland, New Jersey, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia and
South Carolina.&#160;&#160;These dialysis facilities have a total designed
capacity 573 licensed stations.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our 37
dialysis facilities are owned through subsidiaries as follows: 23 wholly-owned
subsidiaries, one of which owns two facilities, and 13 majority-owned
subsidiaries in conjunction with the medical directors of those centers who hold
minority interests.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>One of our Georgia subsidiaries
exercised a call option which resulted in the acquisition of the assets
(effective January 1, 2008) of the Georgia facility we previously
managed.&#160;&#160;We hold an 80% interest in this facility and the former
owner holds the remaining 20% interest.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The company provides acute care
inpatient dialysis services to 11 hospitals in areas serviced by certain of our
dialysis facilities.&#160;&#160;Most of our dialysis facilities have the
capacity to provide training, supplies and on-call support services for home
peritoneal patients.&#160;&#160;Dialysis Corporation of America provided
approximately 272,000 hemodialysis treatments in 2008, an increase of
approximately 20,000 treatments compared to fiscal 2007.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We estimate that on average our centers
were operating at approximately 50% of capacity in December, 2008, based on the
assumption that a dialysis center is able to provide up to three treatments a
day per station, six days a week.&#160;&#160;We believe we can increase the
number of dialysis treatments at most of our centers without making significant
additional capital expenditures.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Operations of Dialysis
Facilities</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our dialysis facilities are designed
specifically for outpatient hemodialysis and generally contain, in addition to
space for dialysis treatments, a nurses&#8217; station, a patient weigh-in area, a
supply room, water treatment space used to purify the water used in hemodialysis
treatments, staff work area, offices, a staff lounge, and a dialyzer
reprocessing room in select facilities (where, with both the patient&#8217;s and
physician&#8217;s consent, the patient&#8217;s dialyzer is sterilized for
reuse).&#160;&#160;Most of our facilities have a designated area for training
patients in home dialysis.&#160;&#160;Each facility also offers amenities for
the patients, such as a color television with headsets for each dialysis
station, to ensure the patients are comfortable and relaxed.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our facilities also offer home
dialysis, primarily continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis and continuous
cycling peritoneal dialysis.&#160;&#160;Training programs for continuous
ambulatory peritoneal dialysis or continuous cycling peritoneal dialysis
generally encompass two to three weeks at the dialysis facility, and such
training is conducted by the facility&#8217;s home training nurse.&#160;&#160;After
the patient completes training, they are able to perform treatment at home with
equipment and supplies provided by the company.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We maintain a team of dialysis
specialists to provide for the individual needs of each patient.&#160;&#160;In
accordance with participation requirements under the Medicare ESRD program, each
facility retains a physician medical director qualified and experienced in the
practice of nephrology and the administration of a renal dialysis
facility.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Physician Relationships&#8221; below.&#160;&#160;Each
facility is overseen by a governing body comprised of an administrator, the
medical director of that facility and the company&#8217;s regional director for that
area.&#160;&#160;The governing body supervises the facility&#8217;s daily operations,
patient care, services necessary for the operation of the facility, and staff,
which consists of registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, patient care
technicians, a social worker to assist the patient and family to adjust to
dialysis treatment and to provide help in financial assistance and planning, and
a registered dietitian.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Employees&#8221; below.&#160;&#160;In
furtherance of our business strategy, we strive to attract and retain skilled
nurses and other staff, for whom competition is intense.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We consider our dialysis equipment to
be both modern and efficient, providing state of the art treatment in a safe and
comfortable environment.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Inpatient Dialysis
Services</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We presently provide inpatient dialysis
services to 11 hospitals in Georgia, Maryland, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Virginia
under agreements either with us or with one of our subsidiaries in the
area.&#160;&#160;The agreements are for terms ranging from one to five years,
some with automatic renewal terms.&#160;&#160;Inpatient services are typically
necessary for patients with acute kidney failure resulting from trauma or
similar causes and ESRD patients who require hospitalization for other
reasons.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Ancillary Services</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our dialysis facilities provide
ancillary services to ESRD patients including the administration of certain
prescription drugs, such as EPO, upon a physician&#8217;s prescription.&#160;&#160;EPO
is a bio-engineered protein which stimulates the production of red blood cells
and is used in connection with dialysis to treat anemia, a medical complication
frequently experienced by ESRD patients.&#160;&#160;EPO decreases the necessity
for blood transfusions in ESRD patients.&#160;&#160;Amgen is the only
manufacturer of EPO in the United States.&#160;&#160;Although we have a good
relationship with this manufacturer and have not experienced any problems in
receipt of our supply of EPO, any loss or limitation of supply of EPO could have
a material adverse effect on patient treatments and our operating revenue and
income.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Amgen has developed an additional
product, darbepoetin alfa, known as Aranesp&#174;.&#160;&#160;Roche has also
developed a drug, Mircera&#174;, used to treat anemia, although it is currently
unavailable to patients in the United States due to Amgen&#8217;s current patent on
EPO.&#160;&#160;These drugs can be administered to patients less frequently than
EPO, which is generally administered to the patient with each dialysis
treatment.&#160;&#160;Although we are unable to predict the impact of these
products on our operations, a significant increase in the development and use of
these alternatives to EPO could have an adverse effect on our revenues, earnings
and cash flow.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Physician Relationships</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>An integral element to the success of a
facility is its association with area nephrologists.&#160;&#160;A dialysis
patient generally seeks treatment at a facility near the patient&#8217;s home and in
proximity to where the patient&#8217;s nephrologist has an established
practice.&#160;&#160;Consequently, we rely on our ability to develop
affiliations with area nephrologists.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The conditions of a facility&#8217;s
participation in the Medicare ESRD program mandate that treatment at a dialysis
facility be under the general supervision of a medical director who is a
physician.&#160;&#160;We retain, by written agreement, qualified physicians or
groups of qualified physicians to serve as medical directors for each of our
facilities.&#160;&#160;Generally, the medical directors are board eligible or
board certified in internal medicine by a professional board specializing in
nephrology and have had at least 12 months of experience in the care of dialysis
patients at ESRD facilities.&#160;&#160;The medical directors are typically a
source of patients treated at the particular center served.&#160;&#160;Our
dialysis centers are operated through subsidiaries, either corporations or
limited liability companies.&#160;&#160;The medical directors of 13 of our
centers, through their affiliated entities, have a minority ownership interest
in the center they service.&#160;&#160;We make every effort to comply with
federal and state regulations concerning our relationship with the physicians
and the medical directors treating patients at our facilities.&#160;&#160;See
&#8220;Government Regulation&#8221; below.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Agreements with medical directors
typically have terms ranging from five to ten years, with renewal provisions,
usually two renewal options each for five years. Each agreement specifies the
duties, responsibilities and compensation of the medical
director.&#160;&#160;Under each agreement, the medical director or professional
association maintains their own medical malpractice insurance.&#160;&#160;The
agreements also typically provide for non-competition in a limited geographic
area surrounding that particular dialysis center during the term of the
agreement and upon termination for a limited period.&#160;&#160;These
agreements, however, do not prohibit physicians providing services at our
facilities from providing direct patient care services at other locations; and
consistent with the federal and state law, such agreements do not require a
physician to refer patients to our dialysis centers.&#160;&#160;Customarily,
physician&#8217;s professional fees for services are billed directly to the patient or
to government payment authorities by the treating physician and paid directly to
the physician or the physician&#8217;s professional association.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our ability to establish and operate a
dialysis facility in a particular area is substantially dependent on the
availability of a qualified nephrologist to serve as the medical
director.&#160;&#160;The loss of a medical director who could not be readily
replaced would have a material adverse effect on the operations of that
facility. In our 33 years of operation, we have not been unable to provide for
or replace a medical director.&#160;&#160;Compensation of medical directors is
separately negotiated for each facility and generally depends on competitive
factors, the size of the facility, and the fair market value of the services to
be provided.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Quality Assurance</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We have implemented a quality assurance
program to maintain and improve the quality of dialysis treatment and care we
provide to our patients in each facility.&#160;&#160;Quality assurance
activities</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">involve
the ongoing examination of care provided, the identification of therapy
deficiencies, the need for any necessary improvements in the quality of care,
and evaluation of improved technology.&#160;&#160;Specifically, this program
requires each center&#8217;s staff, including its medical director and nurse
administrator, to regularly review quality assurance data and initiate programs
for improvement, including dialysis treatment services, equipment, technical and
environmental improvements, and staff-patient and personnel
relationships.&#160;&#160;These evaluations are in addition to assuring
regulatory compliance with CMS and the Occupational Safety and Health
Administration.&#160;&#160;Our Vice President of Clinical Services, a certified
nephrology nurse, oversees this program in addition to ensuring that we meet
federal and state compliance requirements for our dialysis
centers.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Government Regulation&#8221; below.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Quality Clinical Results</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our goal is to provide consistent
quality clinical care to our patients from caring and qualified doctors, nurses,
patient care technicians, social workers and dieticians.&#160;&#160;We have
demonstrated an unwavering commitment to quality renal care through our
continuous quality improvement initiatives.&#160;&#160;We strive to maintain a
leadership position as a quality provider in the dialysis industry and often set
our goals higher than the national average standards.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Kt/V is a formula that measures the
amount of dialysis delivered to the patient, based on the removal of urea, an
end product of protein metabolism.&#160;&#160;Kt/V provides a means to determine
an individual dialysis prescription and to monitor the effectiveness or adequacy
of the dialysis treatment as delivered to the patient.&#160;&#160;We believe it
is critical to achieve a Kt/V level of greater than 1.2 for as many patients as
possible.&#160;&#160;Approximately, 97% of our patients had a Kt/V level greater
than 1.2 for the fourth quarter of 2008 compared to 95% for the fourth quarter
of 2007.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Anemia is a shortage of oxygen-carrying
red blood cells.&#160;&#160;Because red blood cells bring oxygen to all the
cells in the body, untreated anemia can cause severe fatigue, heart disorders,
difficulty concentrating, reduced immune function, and other
problems.&#160;&#160;Anemia is common among renal patients, caused by
insufficient erythropoietin, iron deficiency, repeated blood losses, and other
factors.&#160;&#160;Anemia can be detected with a blood test for hemoglobin or
hematocrit.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>It is
ideal to have as many patients as possible with hemoglobin levels above
11.&#160;&#160;Approximately 82% of our patients had a hemoglobin level greater
than 11 for the fourth quarter of 2008 compared to 79% for the fourth quarter of
2007.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Vascular access is the site on a
patient&#8217;s body where blood is removed and returned during
dialysis.&#160;&#160;CMS has indicated that fistulas are the &#8220;gold standard&#8221; for
establishing access to a patient&#8217;s circulatory system in order to provide
life-sustaining dialysis.&#160;&#160;Approximately 56% of our patients were
dialyzed with a fistula during the fourth quarter of 2008 compared to 53% for
the fourth quarter of 2007.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Patient Revenues</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>A substantial amount of the fees for
outpatient dialysis treatments are funded under the ESRD Program established by
the federal government under the Social Security Act, and administered in
accordance with rates set by CMS.&#160;&#160;A majority of dialysis patients are
covered under Medicare.&#160;&#160;The balance of the outpatient charges are
paid by private payors including the patient&#8217;s medical insurance, private funds
or state Medicaid plans.&#160;&#160;The states in which we operate provide
Medicaid or comparable benefits to qualified recipients to supplement their
Medicare coverage.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under the
ESRD Program, payments for dialysis services are determined pursuant to Part B
of the Medicare Act which presently pays 80% of the allowable charges for each
dialysis treatment furnished to patients.&#160;&#160;The maximum payments vary
based on the geographic location of the center.&#160;&#160;The remaining 20% may
be paid by Medicaid if the patient is eligible, from private insurance funds or
the patient&#8217;s</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
          </div>

        <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always">
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">9</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">personal
funds.&#160;&#160;If there is no payor to cover the remaining 20%, Medicare may
reimburse us for part of that balance as part of our annual cost report
filings.&#160;&#160;Medicare and Medicaid programs are subject to regulatory
changes, statutory limitations and government funding restrictions, which may
adversely affect dialysis services payments and, consequently, our
revenues.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Medicare Reimbursement&#8221; below.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The inpatient dialysis services are
paid for by each contracted hospital pursuant to contractual pre-determined fees
for the different dialysis treatments.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Medicare Reimbursement</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We are reimbursed primarily by Medicare
under a prospective reimbursement system for chronic dialysis services, and by
third party payors including Medicaid and commercial insurance
companies.&#160;&#160;Our dialysis facilities are certified to participate in
the Medicare program.&#160;&#160;Under the Medicare system, the reimbursement
rates are fixed in advance and limit the allowable charge per treatment, but
provide us with predictable and recurring per treatment revenues.&#160;&#160;An
established composite rate set by CMS governs the Medicare reimbursement
available for a designated group of dialysis services, including dialysis
treatments, supplies used for such treatments, and certain laboratory tests and
drugs.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other
ancillary services and items are eligible for separate reimbursement under
Medicare and are not part of the composite rate, including certain drugs such as
EPO, and certain physician-ordered tests provided to dialysis
patients.&#160;&#160;Approximately 27% of our medical services revenue in 2008
was derived from providing dialysis patients with EPO. Effective April, 2006,
and revised again in January, 2008, CMS implemented a policy for monitoring the
dosage of EPO based upon the patient&#8217;s hematocrit level and for limiting the
quantity of EPO that can be administered in any one month.&#160;&#160;This
policy restricts payments based on EPO doses and hemoglobin levels for certain
patients.&#160;&#160;Other ancillary services, mostly other drugs, account for
approximately 10% of our medical services revenue.&#160;&#160;We submit claims
monthly and are usually paid by Medicare within 21 days of the
submission.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There
have been a variety of proposals to Congress for Medicare
reform.&#160;&#160;Congress approved a 1.6% composite rate increase for each of
2005 and 2006, a 1.6% increase which became effective April 1, 2007, and no
increase for 2008.&#160;&#160;For 2008, the drug-add on adjustment to the
composite rate increased 0.6%.&#160;&#160;Medicare reimburses dialysis providers
for the ten most utilized ESRD drugs at an amount equal to the cost of such
drugs, and for other ESRD drugs Medicare reimburses at an amount equal to the
average sale price of the drug as determined by the Inspector General of HHS,
plus 6%, and the composite rate has been increased by an amount estimated by HHS
to be the dialysis provider&#8217;s average profit for these drugs.&#160;&#160;To make
this change budget-neutral, a drug add-on composite was included.&#160;&#160;CMS
reimburses providers using a case mix formula.&#160;&#160;CMS adjusted
reimbursements based on predefined patient parameters such as patient height,
weight and age.&#160;&#160;Congress has mandated a budget neutrality factor
adjustment so that aggregate payments under the system equal payments that would
have been made without the case mix adjustments and the add-on composite for
reimbursement of the drugs.&#160;&#160;Management believes there has been
minimal impact on its average Medicare revenue per treatment as a result of
these changes in Medicare reimbursement.&#160;&#160;Our Medicare composite
payment rate for 2008 was between $127 and $151 per dialysis
treatment.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In July, 2008, Congress passed the
Medicare Improvements for Patients and Providers Act, or MIPPA, which among
other things, provided for a 1% increase in the composite rate in years 2009 and
2010, while also mandating the implementation of a &#8220;bundled&#8221; payment system for
renal dialysis services effective January 1, 2011. The system also will take
into account certain case mix adjustments, including patient weight, body mass
index, comorbidities, length of time on dialysis, age, race, ethnicity and high
cost outliers.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The estimated total amount of payments
under the bundled payment system will be equal to 98% of the estimated total
amount of payments for dialysis services that would have been made with respect
to services furnished in 2011, using the lowest per patient utilization data
from 2007, 2008 and 2009 for estimation purposes.&#160;&#160;Commencing in 2012,
there will be an increase in bundled payment amounts by an ESRD market basket
percentage increase factor that reflects changes over time in prices of an
appropriate mix of goods and services included in the delivery of renal dialysis
services, minus 1%.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In addition, providers will be required
to meet certain quality measures that may include anemia management, patient
satisfaction, iron management, bone mineral metabolism and vascular access.
Commencing January 1, 2012, providers that fail to satisfy such measures will
receive a reduction in the bundled payment rate up to 2%.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Medicaid Reimbursement</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Medicaid programs are state
administered programs partially funded by the federal
government.&#160;&#160;These programs are intended to provide coverage for
patients whose income and assets fall below state defined levels and who are
otherwise uninsured.&#160;&#160;The programs also serve as supplemental
insurance programs for the Medicare co-insurance portion and provide certain
coverages (e.g., oral medications) that are not covered by
Medicare.&#160;&#160;State reimbursements generally follow Medicare
reimbursement levels and coverages without any co-insurance
amounts.&#160;&#160;Certain states, however, require beneficiaries to pay a
monthly share of the cost based upon levels of income or
assets.&#160;&#160;Pennsylvania and New Jersey have Medical Assistance Programs
comparable to Medicaid, with primary and secondary insurance coverage to those
who qualify.</font></div>

of Medical Services Revenue</font><br></div>

equipment, preparing budgets, general accounting, data processing, and other

Program</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We have a Compliance Program to assure
we continue to achieve our goal of providing the highest level of care and
service in a professional and ethical manner consistent with applicable federal
and state laws and regulations.&#160;&#160;This program is intended to (i)
reinforce our management&#8217;s, employees&#8217; and professional affiliates&#8217; awareness of
their responsibilities to comply with applicable laws in the increased and
complex regulatory environment relating to our operations, (ii) benefit the
overall care and services for our dialysis patients, and (iii) assure our

with the law, which, in turn, should assist us in operating in a cost-effective
manner, and accordingly, benefit our shareholders.</font></div>

in compliance with fraud and abuse laws, enhance communication of information,
and provide a mechanism to quickly identify and correct any problems that may
arise.&#160;&#160;This Program supplements and enhances our existing policies,

an audit committee consisting of three independent members of the board who
oversee audits, accounting, financial reporting, and who have established
procedures for receipt, retention and resolution of complaints relating to those
areas, among other responsibilities.&#160;&#160;The audit committee operates
under a charter providing for its detailed responsibilities.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Potential
Liability and Insurance</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Participants in the health care
industry are subject to lawsuits based upon alleged negligence, many of which
involve large claims and significant defense costs.&#160;&#160;We currently have
general and umbrella liability insurance, as well as professional and products
liability.&#160;&#160;Our insurance policies provide coverage on an &#8220;occurrence&#8221;
basis and are subject to annual renewal.&#160;&#160;A hypothetical successful
claim against us in excess of our insurance coverage could have a material
adverse effect upon our business and results of operations.&#160;&#160;The
medical directors supervising our dialysis operations and other physicians
practicing at the facilities are required to maintain their own professional
malpractice insurance coverage.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Government
Regulation</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>General</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Regulation of healthcare facilities,
including dialysis facilities, is extensive, with legislation continually
proposed relating to safety, maintenance of equipment and records, quality
assurance programs, government payment programs and reimbursement rates,
confidentiality of medical records, licensing, patient care and other areas of
operations.&#160;&#160;Each dialysis facility must be certified by CMS, and must
comply with certain rules and regulations established by CMS.&#160;&#160;Each
dialysis facility is also subject to periodic inspections by federal and state
agencies to determine if their operations meet the appropriate regulatory
standards.&#160;&#160;Our operations are also subject to the Occupational Safety
and Health Administration, known as OSHA, relating to workplace safety and
employee exposure to blood and other potentially infectious
material.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Many states have eliminated the
requirement to obtain a certificate of need prior to the establishment or
expansion of a dialysis center.&#160;&#160;There are no certificate of need
requirements in the states in which we are presently operating.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our record of compliance with federal,
state and local governmental laws and regulations remains
excellent.&#160;&#160;Nevertheless, we are unable to predict the scope and
effect of any changes in government regulations, particularly any modifications
in the reimbursement rate for medical services or requirements to obtain
certification from CMS.&#160;&#160;Enforcement, both privately and by the
government, has become more stringent, particularly in attempts to combat fraud
and waste.&#160;&#160;Since our inception in 1976, we continue to maintain our
licenses, including our Medicare and Medicaid and equivalent
certifications.&#160;&#160;The permanent loss of any licenses and certifications
would have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial
position and cash flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
regularly review legislative and regulatory changes and developments and will
restructure a business arrangement if we determine such might place our
operations in material noncompliance with applicable laws or
regulations.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Fraud and Abuse&#8221; and &#8220;Stark II&#8221;
below.&#160;&#160;To date, none of our business arrangements have been the
subject of investigation by any governmental authority.&#160;&#160;No assurance
can be given, however, that our business arrangements will not be the subject of
future investigation or prosecution by federal or state governmental authorities
which could result in civil and/or criminal sanctions.&#160;&#160;Effective
October, 2008, CMS promulgated new regulations revising the conditions of
coverage for ESRD facilities like ours.&#160;&#160;The regulations established
performance expectations for the dialysis facilities and staff, eliminate
certain procedural requirements, and promote continuous quality</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
