      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">improvement
and patient safety measures.&#160;&#160;We have established new Operating
Policies and Procedures with auditing processes to monitor
compliance.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Certification and
Reimbursement</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our dialysis centers must meet certain
requirements, including, among others, those relating to patient care, patient
rights, medical records, the physical set-up of the center, and personnel, in
order to be certified by CMS, to be covered under the Medicare program and to
receive Medicare reimbursement.&#160;&#160;See above under &#8220;Operations &#8211;
Medicare Reimbursement.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Our dialysis centers are certified under the
Medicare program, and are certified under applicable state Medicaid
programs.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Fraud and Abuse</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our dialysis operations are subject to
federal and state laws governing financial relationships between health care
providers and referral sources and the accuracy of information submitted in
connection with reimbursement.&#160;&#160;These laws, collectively referred to
as &#8220;fraud and abuse&#8221; laws, include the Anti-Kickback Statute, Stark II, other
federal fraud laws, and similar state laws.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The fraud
and abuse laws apply because our medical directors have financial relationships
with the dialysis facilities and typically refer patients to those facilities
for items and services reimbursed by federal and state health care
programs.&#160;&#160;Financial relationships with patients who are federal
program beneficiaries also involve the fraud and abuse laws.&#160;&#160;Other
financial relationships which bear scrutiny under the fraud and abuse laws
include relationships with hospitals, nursing homes, and various
vendors.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Anti-Kickback Statutes</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
federal Anti-Kickback Statute prohibits the knowing and willful solicitation,
receipt, offer, or payment of any remuneration, directly or indirectly, in
return for or to induce the referral of patients or the ordering or purchasing
of items or services payable under the Medicare, Medicaid, or other federal
health care program.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Sanctions for violations of the
Anti-Kickback Statute include criminal penalties, such as imprisonment and fines
of up to $25,000 per violation, and civil penalties of up to $50,000 per
violation, as well as mandatory exclusion from Medicare, Medicaid, and other
federal health care programs for a minimum of five years.&#160;&#160;Under U.S.
Sentencing Guidelines, an individual may be fined up to $250,000 and an
organization may be fined up to $500,000 upon conviction of offenses described
in any federal statute.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
language of the Anti-kickback Statute has been construed broadly by the
courts.&#160;&#160;Over the years, the federal government has published
regulations that established &#8220;safe harbors&#8221; to the Anti-Kickback
Statute.&#160;&#160;An arrangement that meets all of the elements of the safe
harbor is immunized from prosecution under the Anti-Kickback
Statute.&#160;&#160;The failure to satisfy all elements, however, does not
necessarily mean the arrangement violates the Anti-Kickback
Statute.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Some states have enacted laws similar
to the Anti-Kickback Statute.&#160;&#160;These laws may apply regardless of
payor source, may include criminal and civil penalties, and may contain
exceptions that differ from the safe harbors to the Anti-Kickback
Statute.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As
required by Medicare regulations, each of our dialysis centers is supervised by
a medical director, who is a licensed nephrologist or otherwise qualified
physician.&#160;&#160;The compensation of each of our medical directors, who are
independent contractors, is fixed by a medical director agreement
and</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always">
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">14</font></div>
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: silver" noshade size="2">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">reflects
competitive factors in each respective location, the size of the center, the
anticipated workload for that particular center, and the physician&#8217;s
professional qualifications.&#160;&#160;The medical director&#8217;s fee is fixed in
advance, typically for periods of one to five years and does not take into
account the volume or value of any referrals to the dialysis
center.&#160;&#160;Thirteen of our outpatient dialysis centers are owned jointly
by us and physicians who hold a minority position through a professional
association.&#160;&#160;These physicians act as the medical directors for those
facilities.&#160;&#160;We attempt to structure our arrangements with our
physicians to comply with the Anti-Kickback Statute with the understanding that
many of these physicians&#8217; patients are treated at our facilities.&#160;&#160;We
believe that the fair market value of the minority interest in a subsidiary
acquired by the physician has been consistent with the cash consideration paid
and/or the assets transferred to the subsidiary, and there is no intent to
induce referrals to any of our centers.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Business &#8211; Physician
Relationships&#8221; above.&#160;&#160;We lease space for six of our centers from
entities in which physicians hold ownership interests.&#160;&#160;We sublease
space to seven of our medical directors at eight of our dialysis
centers.&#160;&#160;These arrangements must be in compliance with the
Anti-Kickback Statute.&#160;&#160;We believe our arrangements with our medical
directors are in compliance with applicable law.&#160;&#160;Several states in
which we operate have laws prohibiting physicians from holding financial
interests in various types of medical facilities.&#160;&#160;If these statutes
are interpreted to apply to relationships we have with our medical directors who
hold a percentage ownership in our dialysis facilities, we would restructure our
relationship with these physicians but could be subject to
penalties.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
believe that the Anti-Kickback Statute and other fraud and abuse laws are
primarily directed at abusive practices that increase the utilization and cost
of services covered by governmentally funded programs.&#160;&#160;The dialysis
services we provide generally cannot, by their very nature, be over-utilized
since dialysis treatment is not elective, and is only indicated when there is
temporary or permanent kidney failure.&#160;&#160;Medical necessity is capable
of being supported by objective documentation, drastically reducing the
possibility of over-utilization.&#160;&#160;Additionally, there are safe harbors
for certain arrangements.&#160;&#160;Nevertheless, while relationships created
by medical director ownership of minority interests in our facilities satisfy
many but not all of the criteria for the safe harbor, there can be no assurance
that these relationships will not subject us to investigation or prosecution by
enforcement agencies.&#160;&#160;In an effort to further our compliance with the
law, we have adopted a corporate Compliance Program that addresses medical
necessity and medical chart audits to confirm medical necessity of
referrals.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>With respect to our inpatient dialysis
services, we provide hospitals with dialysis services, including qualified
nursing and technical personnel, supplies, equipment and technical
services.&#160;&#160;In certain instances, the medical director of our dialysis
center who has a minority interest in that facility may refer patients to
hospitals with which we have an inpatient dialysis services
arrangement.&#160;&#160;We believe our acute inpatient hospital services are in
compliance with the law.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Stark II&#8221; below.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
endeavor in good faith to comply with all governmental
regulations.&#160;&#160;However, there can be no assurance that we will not be
required to change our practices or experience a material adverse effect as a
result of any such potential challenge.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict the outcome
of the rule-making process, enforcement procedures, or whether changes in the
safe harbor rules will affect our position with respect to the Anti-Kickback
Statute, but we will continue to make every effort to remain in
compliance.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Stark II</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The federal physician self referral
law, commonly known as Stark II, prohibits a physician who has a financial
relationship, or who has an immediate family member who has a financial
relationship, with entities providing &#8220;designated health services&#8221; from
referring Medicare or Medicaid patients to such entity for such services unless
an exception applies.&#160;&#160;A &#8220;financial relationship&#8221; includes an
ownership or investment interest in, or a compensation arrangement between the
physician and the entity.&#160;&#160;For purposes of Stark II, &#8220;designated
health services&#8221; include clinical laboratory services, durable medical
equipment,</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always">
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">15</font></div>
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: silver" noshade size="2">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">parenteral
and enteral nutrients, home health services, and inpatient and outpatient
hospital services.&#160;&#160;Dialysis treatments are not &#8220;designated health
services.&#8221;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
self-referral prohibition has numerous exceptions, including exceptions for
personal service arrangements, leases of space and equipment, employment
relationships and referrals within group practices.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">An entity
is prohibited from submitting Medicare or Medicaid claims for services furnished
pursuant to an unlawful referral and must refund amounts received pursuant to
prohibited referrals.&#160;&#160;Violators are subject to civil monetary
penalties of up to $15,000 for each improper claim and may be excluded from
participation in the Medicare and Medicaid programs.&#160;&#160;Unlike the
federal Anti-Kickback Statute, intent to violate the law is not
required.&#160;&#160;Knowing violations of Stark II may also serve as the basis
for liability under the False Claims Act.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;False Claims Act&#8221;
below.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>HHS regulations to Stark II became
effective in January, 2002.&#160;&#160;CMS adopted Phase II of its regulations
under Stark II in March, 2004.&#160;&#160;These regulations exclude from covered
designated health services and referral prohibitions, services included in the
ESRD composite rate and EPO and other drugs required as part of dialysis
treatments under certain conditions.&#160;&#160;Also excluded from &#8220;inpatient
hospital services&#8221; are dialysis services provided by a hospital not certified by
CMS to provide outpatient dialysis services, which would exclude our inpatient
hospital services agreements from Stark II.&#160;&#160;Equipment and supplies
used in connection with home dialysis are excluded from the Stark II definition
of &#8220;durable medical equipment.&#8221;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Stark II regulations and the
legislative history of Stark II indicate that the purpose behind the Stark II
prohibition on physician referral is to prevent Medicare and Medicaid program
and patient abuse.&#160;&#160;Since dialysis is a necessary medical treatment
for those with temporary or permanent kidney failure, it is not highly
susceptible to that type of abuse.&#160;&#160;We believe, based upon current
rules and the industry practice, Congress did not intend to include dialysis
services and the services and items we provide that are incidental to dialysis
services within the Stark II prohibitions.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If the
provisions of Stark II were found to apply to our arrangements however, we
believe that we would be in compliance.&#160;&#160;We compensate our medical
directors pursuant to medical director agreements, which we believe meet the
exception for personal service arrangements under Stark II.&#160;&#160;No other
physicians who send their patients to or treat their patients at any of our
facilities receive compensation from us.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Medical directors of our dialysis
centers who hold a minority investment interest in the subsidiaries operating
those centers may refer patients to hospitals with which we have an acute
inpatient dialysis service arrangement.&#160;&#160;Although the regulations of
Stark II may be interpreted to apply to these types of transactions, we believe
that our contractual arrangements with hospitals for acute care inpatient
dialysis services are in compliance with Stark II.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>A limited number of dialysis facilities
are leased from entities in which physicians hold ownership interests, and we
sublease space to seven of our medical directors.&#160;&#160;Stark II provides
an exception for these types of affiliated physician lease agreements if
specific requirements are met.&#160;&#160;The company believes these leases
satisfy the requirements for these exceptions.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>If CMS or any other government entity
otherwise interprets the Stark II regulations, we may be required to restructure
certain existing compensation or investment agreements with our medical
directors, or, in the alternative, refuse to accept referrals for designated
health services from certain physicians.&#160;&#160;Stark II prohibits Medicare
or Medicaid reimbursement of items or services provided</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always">
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">16</font></div>
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: silver" noshade size="2">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">pursuant
to a prohibited referral, and imposes substantial civil monetary penalties on
facilities which submit claims for reimbursement for such prohibited
referrals.&#160;&#160;If such were to be the case, we could be required to repay
amounts reimbursed for drugs, equipment and services that CMS determines to have
been furnished in violation of Stark II, in addition to substantial civil
monetary penalties, which could adversely affect our operations and financial
results.&#160;&#160;We believe that if Stark II is interpreted by CMS or any
other governmental entity to apply to our arrangements, it is possible that we
could be permitted to bring our financial relationships with referring
physicians into material compliance with the provisions of Stark II on a
prospective basis.&#160;&#160;However, prospective compliance may not eliminate
the amounts or penalties, if any, that might be determined to be owed for past
conduct, and there can be no assurance that the costs and expenses associated
with such prospective compliance, if permissible, would not have a material
adverse effect on our results of operation, financial position or cash
flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">False
Claims Act</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The False
Claims Act is the federal government&#8217;s primary civil remedy for improper or
fraudulent claims.&#160;&#160;It applies to all federal programs, including
Medicare and Medicaid.&#160;&#160;The False Claims Act prohibits, among other
things, (1) knowingly presenting or causing to be presented a false or
fraudulent claim, (2) knowingly making or using, or causing to be made or used,
a false record or statement in order to have a false or fraudulent claim paid,
(3) conspiring to defraud the government by getting a false or fraudulent claim
allowed or paid, and (4) knowingly making or using, or causing to be made or
used, a false record or statement to conceal, avoid, or decrease an obligation
to pay the government.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#8220;Knowingly&#8221;
means that a person, with respect to information:&#160;&#160;(1) has actual
knowledge of the information; (2) acts in deliberate ignorance of the truth or
falsity of the information; or (3) acts in reckless disregard of the truth or
falsity of the information.&#160;&#160;No proof of specific intent to defraud is
required.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Penalties
for violation of the False Claims Act include fines of $5,500 to $11,000 per
false claim, plus treble damages.&#160;&#160;Prosecution under the False Claims
Act involves an extensive variety of alleged false claims and fraud allegedly
perpetrated against Medicare and state healthcare programs, including billing
for services not rendered, coding errors, the submission of false cost reports,
and billing for services at a higher payment rate than
appropriate.&#160;&#160;The federal government can use other criminal federal
statutes to prosecute false claims.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
Corporate Compliance Program is designed to address risks inherent in the
submission of claims and other information in connection with the Medicare and
Medicaid program and we are committed to ensuring the accuracy of all
claims.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance, however, that we will not be
subject to an investigation or audit regarding the accuracy of any claim or
other information submitted in connection with our operations. </font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>HIPAA</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Health Insurance Portability and
Accountability Act of 1996, known as HIPAA, provided for health insurance
reforms which included a variety of provisions important to healthcare
providers, such as significant changes to the Medicare and Medicaid fraud and
abuse laws.&#160;&#160;HIPAA established two programs that coordinate federal,
state and local healthcare fraud and abuse activities.&#160;&#160;Under these
programs, these governmental entities undertake a variety of monitoring
activities, including medical utilization and fraud review, cost report audits
and secondary payor determinations.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always">
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">17</font></div>
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: silver" noshade size="2">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>As part of the administrative
simplification provisions of HIPAA, there are regulations governing electronic
transactions relating to healthcare information.&#160;&#160;These regulations
require a party transmitting or receiving healthcare transactions electronically
to send and receive data in single format.&#160;&#160;This regulation applies to
our submissions and processing of healthcare claims and also applies to many of
our payors.&#160;&#160;We believe that we are in compliance with the
transactions standards rule.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>HIPAA also includes provisions relating
to the privacy of healthcare information.&#160;&#160;HHS&#8217; privacy rules cover
all individually identifiable healthcare information known as &#8220;protected health
information&#8221; and apply to healthcare providers, health plans, and healthcare
clearing houses, known as &#8220;covered entities.&#8221;&#160;&#160;The regulations are
quite extensive and complex, but basically require companies to: (i) obtain
patient acknowledgement of receipt of a notice of privacy practices; (ii) obtain
patient authorization before certain uses and disclosures of protected health
information; (iii) respond to patient requests for access to their healthcare
information; and (iv) develop policies and procedures with respect to uses and
disclosures of protected health information.&#160;&#160;We believe we are in
compliance with the HIPAA privacy rules.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>HIPAA has security regulations
governing the security of health information that is maintained or transmitted
electronically.&#160;&#160;These regulations generally require implementation of
safeguards for ensuring the confidentiality of electronic health
information.&#160;&#160;Management believes it is currently in compliance with
the HIPAA security standards.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">HIPAA
expressly prohibits four practices, namely (1) submitting a claim that the
person knows or has reason to know is for medical items or services that are not
medically necessary, (2) transferring remuneration to Medicare and Medicaid
beneficiaries that is likely to influence such beneficiary to order or receive
items or services, (3) certifying the need for home health services knowing that
all of the coverage requirements have not been met, and (4) engaging in a
pattern or practice of upcoding claims in order to obtain greater
reimbursement.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As for
criminal penalties, HIPAA adds healthcare fraud, theft, embezzlement,
obstruction of investigations and false statements to the general federal
criminal code with respect to federally funded health programs, thus subjecting
such acts to criminal penalties.&#160;&#160;Persons convicted of these crimes
face up to 10 years imprisonment and/or fines.&#160;&#160;Moreover, a court
imposing a sentence on a person convicted of federal healthcare offense may
order the person to forfeit all real or personal property that is derived from
the criminal offense.&#160;&#160;The Attorney General is also provided with a
greatly expanded subpoena power under HIPAA to investigate fraudulent criminal
activities, and federal prosecutors may utilize asset freezes, injunctive relief
and forfeiture of proceeds to limit fraud during such an
investigation.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Although we believe we substantially
comply with currently applicable state and federal laws and regulations and to
date have not had any difficulty in maintaining our licenses and Medicare and
Medicaid authorizations, the healthcare service industry is and will continue to
be subject to substantial and continually changing regulation at the federal and
state levels, and the scope and effect of such and its impact on our operations
cannot be predicted.&#160;&#160;No assurance can be given that our activities
will not be reviewed or challenged by regulatory authorities.&#160;&#160;We
continue to work with our healthcare counsel in reviewing our policies and
procedures and make every effort to comply with HIPAA and other applicable
federal and state laws and regulations.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Environmental and Health
Regulations</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our dialysis centers are subject to
various federal, state and local hazardous waste laws and non-hazardous medical
waste disposal laws.&#160;&#160;Most of our waste is
non-hazardous.&#160;&#160;We also follow OSHA&#8217;s Hazardous Waste Communications
Policy, which requires all employees to be knowledgeable of the</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
          </div>

          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: silver" noshade size="2">

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">presence
of and familiar with the use and disposal of hazardous chemicals in the
facility.&#160;&#160;Medical waste of each facility is handled by licensed local
medical waste sanitation agencies who are responsible for compliance with such
laws.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>There are a variety of regulations
promulgated under OSHA relating to employees exposed to blood and other
potentially infectious materials requiring employers, including dialysis
centers, to provide protection.&#160;&#160;We adhere to OSHA&#8217;s protective
guidelines, including regularly testing employees and patients for exposure to
hepatitis B and providing employees subject to such exposure with hepatitis B
vaccinations on an as-needed basis, protective equipment, a written exposure
control plan and training in infection control and waste disposal.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other
Regulation</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The company complies with the employee
education processes of the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Certain states have Anti-Kickback
legislation and laws dealing with self-referral provisions similar to the
federal Anti-Kickback Statute and Stark II.&#160;&#160;We have no reason to
believe that we are not in compliance with such state laws.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our&#160;Compliance
Program is designed to assure compliance with fraud and abuse laws and
regulations.&#160;&#160;See above under the caption &#8220;Compliance
Program.&#8221;&#160;&#160;The establishment and implementation of our Compliance
Program, coupled with our existing policies and internal controls, could have
the effect of mitigating any civil or criminal penalties for potential
violations.&#160;&#160;We will continue to use our best efforts to fully comply
with federal and state laws, regulations and requirements as applicable to our
operations and business.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Medical
Products</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Subsequent to our merger in September,
2005, with our former parent company, Medicore, Inc., we became engaged in the
distribution of medical products, primarily disposables and diabetic supplies,
both domestically and internationally, to hospitals, blood banks, laboratories
and retail pharmacies.&#160;&#160;We distribute blood lancets used to draw blood
for testing under the names Producers of Quality Medical Disposables&#8482;, Lady
Lite&#8482;, our brand name Lite Touch, or under a private label if requested by the
customer.&#160;&#160;Medical devices are required by the FDA, as a condition of
marketing, to secure a 510(k) premarket notification clearance or a Premarket
Approval Application.&#160;&#160;A product will be cleared by the FDA under a
510(k) if it is found to be substantially equivalent in terms of safety,
effectiveness and intended use to another legally marketed
product.&#160;&#160;We received 510(k) clearance for our blood lancet line and
insulin syringes.&#160;&#160;Our medical products are subject to continuing FDA
oversight, including labeling, &#8220;good manufacturing practices,&#8221; as defined in FDA
regulations, and adverse event reporting, none of which adverse events have
occurred to date.&#160;&#160;Marketing of our medical products is conducted by
our employees and independent manufacturer representatives.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Competition</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The dialysis industry is highly
competitive.&#160;&#160;There are numerous providers who have dialysis centers
in the same areas as our centers.&#160;&#160;Many are owned by larger
corporations, which operate dialysis centers regionally, nationally and
internationally.&#160;&#160;Our operations are small in comparison with those
corporations.&#160;&#160;Two of our major competitors are significantly larger
public companies, Fresenius Medical Care, Inc., and DaVita,
Inc.&#160;&#160;These companies have substantially greater financial resources,
significantly more centers, patients and services than we do, and by virtue of
such may have an advantage over us in</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">

          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">19</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">competing
for nephrologists and acquisitions of dialysis facilities in areas and markets
we target.&#160;&#160;Moreover, competition for acquisitions has increased the
cost of acquiring existing dialysis centers.&#160;&#160;Fresenius also
manufactures and sells dialysis equipment and supplies, which may provide it
with a greater competitive edge.&#160;&#160;We also face competition from
hospitals and physicians that operate their own dialysis
facilities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Competitive factors most important in
dialysis treatment are quality of care and service, convenience of location and
pleasantness of the environment.&#160;&#160;Another significant competitive
factor is the ability to attract and retain qualified
nephrologists.&#160;&#160;These physicians are required as medical directors of
the dialysis center for it to participate in the Medicare ESRD program, and are
responsible for the supervision of the medical operations of the
center.&#160;&#160;Our medical directors usually are subject to non-compete
restrictions within a limited geographic area from the center they
administer.&#160;&#160;They can be a substantial source of patients for the
centers.&#160;&#160;Additionally, there is always substantial competition for
obtaining qualified, competent nurses and technical staff at reasonable labor
costs.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that we will compete
effectively.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The medical products industry is
extremely competitive and our medical products operations are not a significant
competitive factor in this area.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Employees</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>As of March 13, 2009, we had 550 full
time employees, including administrators, licensed practical nurses, registered
nurses, technical specialists, patient care technicians, clerical employees,
social workers, dietitians, corporate staff and four employees in the medical
products operations.&#160;&#160;We retain 38 part-time employees consisting of
registered nurses, patient care technicians and clerical
employees.&#160;&#160;We also utilize 149 per diem personnel to supplement
staffing.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We retain nine independent contractors,
including social workers and dietitians at various of our dialysis
facilities.&#160;&#160;These contractors are in addition to the medical
directors, who supervise patient treatment at each facility.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

employees are excellent and we have not suffered any strikes or work
stoppages.&#160;&#160;None of our employees are represented by any labor
union.&#160;&#160;We are an equal opportunity employer.</font></div>

complex and open to further judicial and legislative
interpretations.&#160;&#160;If we are forced to change our method of operations
because of these regulations, our earnings, financial condition and business
could be adversely affected.&#160;&#160;The imposition of additional licensing
and other regulatory requirements may, among other things, increase our cost of
doing business.&#160;&#160;In addition, any violation of these governmental
regulations could involve substantial civil and criminal penalties and fines,
revocation of our licenses, closure of one or more of our centers, and our
exclusion from participating in Medicare and Medicaid programs.&#160;&#160;Any
loss of federal or state certifications or licenses would materially adversely
impact our business.</font></div>

arrangements with our physician medical directors do not meet the safe harbor
provisions of federal and state laws, and may subject us to greater governmental
scrutiny</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Neither our arrangements with the
medical directors of our facilities, typically retained by us as independent
contractors under a fixed fee medical director agreement, nor the minority
ownership interests of physicians in certain of our dialysis facilities meet all
of the requirements of safe harbors to the Anti-Kickback Statute and similar
state laws.&#160;&#160;These laws impose civil and criminal sanctions on persons
who receive or make payments for referring a patient for treatment that is paid
for in whole or in part by Medicare, Medicaid or similar state
programs.&#160;&#160;Transactions and arrangements involving physician minority
ownership that do not fall within a safe harbor may be subject to greater
scrutiny by enforcement agencies, and if determined to violate the Anti-Kickback
Statute or Stark II law could subject us to repayment of certain reimbursement
amounts, monetary penalties and exclusion from further participation in
government programs.&#160;&#160;If we are unable to modify the arrangement to
satisfy the applicable laws and safe-harbor provisions, we would not be allowed
to accept patient referrals from the physician with whom we have the
arrangement.&#160;&#160;In any of these circumstances, our financial position,
results of operations and cash flows would be adversely affected.</font></div>

implemented by Congress in recent years, including modest percentage increases
in the Medicare composite rate (the fixed payment rate for a dialysis treatment
including related supplies, laboratory tests and pharmaceuticals) while at the
same time modifying the bases by which CMS reimburses for separately billable
services and pharmaceuticals, such as EPO, did not, in the aggregate,
significantly impact our cash flows, results of operations or financial
position.&#160;&#160;Nevertheless, the government has continued to review the
processes for reimbursement of dialysis services and in July, 2008, Congress
passed the Medicare Improvements for Patients and Providers Act which, while
providing for marginal increases in the composite rate for 2009 and 2010,
establishes&#160;&#160;&#8220;bundled&#8221;&#160;&#160;payments for all goods and services
provided during the dialysis treatment beginning in 2011 at an initial rate set
at 2% below the payment rate that providers historically received under prior
methodologies.&#160;&#160;&#160;From and after 2012, although the new single
bundled payment base rate will be adjusted annually for inflation</font></div>

upon a market basket index less 1% of such index, the bundled payment rate will

generally.&#160;&#160;Some of these commercial payors are increasingly

non-governmental third-party organizations would adversely affect our

result in a reduction of revenue.&#160;&#160;We estimate approximately 39%, 43%
and 46% of our patient revenues for 2006, 2007 and 2008, respectively, was
obtained from sources other than Medicare or Medicaid and equivalent
programs.&#160;&#160;We generally charge non-governmental organizations for
dialysis treatment rates which exceed the fixed Medicare and Medicaid and
equivalent rates.&#160;&#160;If commercial payors reduce their payments or we

upon a payor mix balance that has reflected an increase in recent years of
revenues from commercial payor reimbursement.&#160;&#160;To the extent, however,
that the current economic slowdown and financial crisis affecting the United
States persists for an extended period of time, we may face a number of
potential effects that could materially impact our revenues, earnings and
financial condition.&#160;&#160;In particular, continued increases in job losses

based programs.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, employers facing operating cost

reimbursement payments for our services to the extent that economic conditions
continue to worsen.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Any
decrease in the availability of or the reimbursement rate of EPO would reduce
our revenues and earnings</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>EPO is currently available from a
single manufacturer, Amgen, Inc.&#160;&#160;The available supply of EPO could be
delayed or reduced, whether by Amgen itself, through unforeseen circumstances,
or as a result of excessive demand.&#160;&#160;In addition, Amgen could increase
the price of EPO.&#160;&#160;This could adversely impact our revenues and
profitability, since approximately 28% of our medical services revenues in 2006,
27% in 2007 and 27% in 2008 were based upon the administration of EPO to our
dialysis patients.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Most of our EPO reimbursement is from
government programs.&#160;&#160;For 2008, 68% of total EPO revenue was derived
from Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement.&#160;&#160;In recent years, CMS
revised its rules for reimbursement of pharmaceuticals, including EPO, which
resulted in a net reduction of average Medicare payment rates.&#160;&#160;In
2006, reimbursement for EPO was at the average sales price plus 6%, which
resulted in lower reimbursement for pharmaceuticals, but was offset by the 1.6%
composite rate increase.&#160;&#160;If government or commercial payors further
reduce reimbursement for EPO, then our revenues and earnings per treatment may
decline.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Further
changes and rules intended to address EPO and other pharmaceuticals could
adversely affect our revenues and income.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Changes in Medicare reimbursement
criteria have impacted EPO revenue.&#160;&#160;CMS implemented a national
monitoring policy for EPO claims in April, 2006, which aimed to reduce
reimbursement for EPO utilization above a certain hemotacrit threshold in a
patient.&#160;&#160;The policy also limited the quantity of EPO that could be
administered in a month, regardless of hematocrit levels.&#160;&#160;We revised
our protocols on anemia management to address this policy and did not incur an
adverse impact on our results of operations.&#160;&#160;Nevertheless, since the
latter part of 2006 a significant amount of government and media attention has
been paid to the management of anemia generally in all fields of medicine
resulting in congressional hearings and FDA required label changes to EPO and
Aranesp<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#174;</font>
which have been and are continuing to be examined.&#160;&#160;In January, 2008,
CMS put into effect additional changes to its EPO monitoring policy intended to
further limit reimbursement.&#160;&#160;Commercial payors may also follow suit
as they direct greater scrutiny to their policies for EPO use as part of their
overall analysis of dialysis services reimbursement.&#160;&#160;Further changes
in EPO administration policies that result in further restrictions on
utilization could result in a decline in our revenues and earnings per
treatment.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">New
drugs could affect use of EPO, adversely impacting our
profitability.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Amgen is the sole manufacturer of EPO,
which is administered in conjunction with dialysis treatments to address a
patient&#8217;s anemia.&#160;&#160;Amgen has developed the drug Aranesp&#174;, and Roche
has developed Mircera&#174;, each of which can be used to treat anemia, and which are
indicated to be effective for longer periods than EPO.&#160;&#160;Based on their
longer lasting capabilities, potential margins on these alternative
pharmaceuticals could be significantly lower than on EPO, and furthermore, their
potential for being administered by a dialysis patient&#8217;s physician, could
further eliminate potential revenues from the treatment of anemia in our
dialysis patients.&#160;&#160;The introduction and marketing of alternative
pharmaceuticals as an anemia treatment for dialysis patients, could adversely
impact our results of operations, financial position or cash
flows.&#160;&#160;Currently, Mircera&#174; is not available for use in the United
States due to a patent held by Amgen.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Disruptions
or inefficiencies in the supply chain, particularly with pharmaceuticals, could
negatively impact our earnings and financial condition</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Last year Baxter Healthcare Corporation
engaged in a recall of heparin, a pharmaceutical used in the provision of
dialysis services, and shortly thereafter ceased further sales of this
pharmaceutical altogether, leaving one supplier of heparin in the United
States.&#160;&#160;The price for heparin has since increased nearly four-fold
and may continue to rise in the future.&#160;&#160;While we do not believe,
given our historical utilization of heparin, that the current price will
materially affect our earnings, continued increases in the price, or limitations
on the availability of this pharmaceutical could negatively impact our
operations and earnings.&#160;&#160;Similarly, while we rely on a number of
vendors for our dialysis supplies and pharmaceuticals, to the extent that such
supply were disrupted for an extended period of time, our inability to identify
and establish a cost-effective replacement could significantly impact our
operations, earnings and financial position.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
ability to grow is subject to our resources and available locations</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Over the past several years we have
both built and acquired several dialysis centers, in some cases with partners
holding a minority interest.&#160;&#160;We seek areas with qualified and
cost-effective nursing and technical personnel and a sufficient population to
sustain a dialysis center.&#160;&#160;These opportunities are limited and we
compete with much larger dialysis companies for appropriate
locations.&#160;&#160;Our growth strategy based on construction also involves
the risks of our ability to identify suitable locations to develop additional
centers.&#160;&#160;Those we do develop may never achieve profitability, and
additional financing may not be available to finance future
development.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our inability to acquire or develop
dialysis centers in a cost-effective manner would adversely affect our ability
to expand our business and as a result, our profitability.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Growth places significant demands on
our financial and management skills.&#160;&#160;Inability on our behalf to meet
the challenges of expansion and to manage any such growth would have an adverse
effect on our results of operations, financial position or cash
flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
attempt to expand through development or acquisition of dialysis centers which
are not currently identified entails risks which shareholders and investors will
not have a basis to evaluate</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We expand generally by seeking an
appropriate location for a dialysis center and by taking into consideration the
potential geographic patient base, types of commercial insurance in the area,
the availability of a physician nephrologist to be our medical director, and a
skilled work force.&#160;&#160;Construction, equipment and initial working
capital costs for a new dialysis center with 15 stations, typically the size of
our dialysis facilities, range from $1,000,000 to $1,500,000.&#160;&#160;While
and acquisition of existing outpatient dialysis centers is a faster means for
achieving profitability, these transactions can be more
costly.&#160;&#160;Therefore, the company takes a selective approach to its
acquisition strategy.&#160;&#160;We cannot assure you that we will be successful
in developing or acquiring dialysis facilities, or otherwise successfully
expanding our operations.&#160;&#160;We are routinely negotiating with
nephrologists and others to establish new dialysis centers, but we cannot assure
you that these negotiations will result in the development of new
centers.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, there is no basis for shareholders and
investors to evaluate the specific merits or risks of any potential development
or acquisition of dialysis facilities.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
depend on physician referrals, and the limitation or cessation of such referrals
would adversely impact our revenues and earnings</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Most dialysis facilities, including
ours, are dependent upon referrals of ESRD patients for treatment by physicians,
primarily those physicians specializing in nephrology.&#160;&#160;We retain by
written agreement qualified physicians or groups of qualified physicians to
serve as medical directors for each of our facilities. The medical directors are
typically a source of patients treated at the particular facility
served.&#160;&#160;There is no requirement for these physicians to refer their
patients to us, and they are free to refer patients to any other dialysis
facility.&#160;&#160;The loss of the patient base of the medical director or
other physicians in the area of our facilities could result in a decline in our
operations, revenues and earnings.&#160;&#160;We may not be able to renew or
otherwise negotiate compensation under the medical director agreements with our
medical director physicians which could terminate the relationship, and without
a suitable medical director replacement could result in closure of the
facility.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the loss of these key physicians at a
particular facility could have a material adverse effect on the operations of
the facility and could adversely affect our revenues and
earnings.&#160;&#160;Most of our medical director agreements range in terms of
from five to ten years with renewals, and we have had no difficulty in renewing
agreements as they have expired.&#160;&#160;All the medical director agreements
provide for noncompetition restrictions.&#160;&#160;We have never had to attempt
to enforce such restrictions, but there is no assurance that a particular
jurisdiction in which the agreement is applicable would uphold such
noncompetition agreement, which would increase the potential for competition
with affiliated dialysis centers and could adversely impact our revenues and
earnings.</font></div>

medical groups with whom they are associated own minority interests in certain
of our subsidiaries which operate dialysis centers.&#160;&#160;If these
interests are deemed to violate applicable federal or state law, these
physicians may be forced to dispose of their ownership interests.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Industry
changes could adversely affect our business</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Healthcare organizations, public and
private, continue to change the manner in which they operate and pay for
services.&#160;&#160;Our business is designed to function within the current
healthcare financing and reimbursement system.&#160;&#160;In recent years, the
healthcare industry has been subject to increasing levels of government
regulation of reimbursement rates and capital expenditures, among other
things.&#160;&#160;In addition, proposals to reform the healthcare system have
been considered by Congress, and still remain a priority issue.&#160;&#160;Any
new legislative initiatives, if enacted, may (i) further increase government
regulation of or other involvement in healthcare, (ii) lower reimbursement
rates, and (iii) otherwise change the operating environment for healthcare
companies.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict the likelihood of those events or what
impact they may have on our results of operation, financial position or cash
flows.</font></div>

competitive environment in terms of the operation, development and acquisition
of dialysis centers.&#160;&#160;Our competition comes from other dialysis
centers, many of which are owned by much larger companies, and from
hospitals.&#160;&#160;We also compete with physicians who open their own
dialysis facilities.&#160;&#160;The dialysis industry is rapidly consolidating,
resulting in several large dialysis companies competing for the acquisition of
existing dialysis centers and the development of relationships with referring
physicians.&#160;&#160;Some of our competitors have significantly greater
financial resources, more dialysis facilities and a significantly larger patient
base.&#160;&#160;Competition for acquiring existing centers has increased the
costs of acquiring such facilities.</font></div>

of operations in the healthcare services industry has increased, resulting not

&#8220;Business &#8211; Operations &#8211; Location, Capacity and Use of Facilities&#8221;
above.&#160;&#160;The existing dialysis facilities could accommodate greater

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>At March 11, 2009, we had 898

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Dividend
Policy</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We have not declared or paid cash
dividends to our shareholders, and we do not anticipate paying dividends in the
foreseeable future.&#160;&#160;The board of directors intends to retain earnings
to finance our growth strategy.&#160;&#160;Future dividend policy will be at the
discretion of the board of directors, and will depend on our earnings, capital
requirements, financial condition and other similar relevant
factors.&#160;&#160;Any determination to pay a dividend is also subject to the
covenants in the KeyBank National Association credit facility (see Item 7,
&#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of
Operations,&#8221; which precludes the payment of any dividends (other than stock
dividends), as does the mortgage on our Valdosta, Georgia property (see Item 2,
&#8220;Properties&#8221;) which restricts the payment of dividends above 25% of our net
worth.</font></div>

                <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Management's

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of
Financial Condition and Results of Operations, commonly known as MD&amp;A, is
our attempt to provide a narrative explanation of our financial statements, and
to provide our shareholders and investors with the dynamics of our business as
seen through our eyes as management.&#160;&#160;Generally, MD&amp;A is intended
to cover expected effects of known or reasonably expected uncertainties,
expected effects of known trends on future operations, and prospective effects
of events that have had a material effect on past operating
results.&#160;&#160;Our discussion of MD&amp;A should be read in conjunction
with our consolidated financial statements, including the notes, included
elsewhere in this annual report on Form 10-K.&#160;&#160;Please also review the
Cautionary Notice Regarding Forward-Looking Information on page one of this
annual report.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Overview</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We provide dialysis services, primarily
kidney dialysis treatments through 37 outpatient dialysis centers, including one
center acquired on December 31, 2008, one center acquired effective January 1,
2008, and one new center opened during 2008, to patients with chronic kidney
failure, also known as end-stage renal disease or ESRD.&#160;&#160;We provide
dialysis treatments to dialysis patients of 11 hospitals and medical centers
through acute inpatient dialysis services agreements with those
entities.&#160;&#160;We provide homecare services, including home peritoneal
dialysis.&#160;&#160;We engage in medical product sales, which is not a
significant part of our business.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Quality
Clinical Results</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our goal is to provide consistent
quality clinical care to our patients from caring and qualified doctors, nurses,
patient care technicians, social workers and dieticians.&#160;&#160;We have
demonstrated an unwavering commitment to quality renal care through our
continuous quality improvement initiatives.&#160;&#160;We strive to maintain a
leadership position as a quality provider in the dialysis industry and often set
our goals to exceed the national average standards.&#160;&#160;See Item 1,
&#8220;Business &#8211; Operations &#8211; Quality Clinical Results.&#8221;</font></div>
