        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">December
31, 2008</font></div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center">&#160;</div>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE
1--SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES&#8212;Continued</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Estimated
Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The carrying value of cash and cash
equivalents, accounts receivable, prepaid expenses and other current assets and
accounts payable and accrued expenses in the accompanying financial statements
approximate their fair value because of the short-term maturity of these
instruments.&#160;&#160;Debt approximates fair value since such instruments
either bear variable interest rates which approximate market or have interest
rates approximating those currently available to us for loans with similar terms
and maturities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Reclassification</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Certain prior year amounts have been
reclassified to conform with the current year&#8217;s presentation.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">New
Pronouncements</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In September, 2006, the Financial
Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Statement of Financial Accounting
Standards No. 157 (SFAS 157), &#8220;Fair Value Measurements.&#8221;&#160;&#160;SFAS 157
defines fair value, establishes a framework for measuring fair value in
generally accepted accounting principles, and expands disclosures about fair
value measurements.&#160;&#160;SFAS 157 applies under other accounting
pronouncements that require fair value measurement in which the FASB concluded
that fair value was the relevant measurement, but does not require any new fair
value measurements.&#160;&#160;We adopted SFAS 157 effective January 1, 2008,
except for the nonfinancial assets and liabilities that are subject to a
one-year deferral allowed by FASB Staff Position (FSP) FAS 157-2 (FSP FAS157-2),
&#8220;Effective Date of FASB Statement No. 157&#8221; issued February 12,
2008.&#160;&#160;The standard applies to assets and liabilities that are carried
at fair value on a recurring basis.&#160;&#160;FSP FAS157-2 delays the effective
date of SFAS 157 until fiscal years beginning after November 15, 2008 for
nonfinancial assets and liabilities that are not recognized or disclosed at fair
value in the financial statements on a recurring basis (at least
annually).&#160;&#160;The adoption of SFAS 157 did not have a material effect on
our financial statements.&#160;&#160;We are evaluating the impact SFAS 157 will
have on our financial statements beginning in fiscal 2009 as it relates to the
items subject to the one-year deferral allowed by FSP FAS 157-2.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In December, 2007, the FASB issued
Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 141 (revised 2007) (SFAS 141R),
&#8220;Business Combinations.&#8221;&#160;&#160;SFAS 141R expands the definitions of a
business and business combination and requires all assets and liabilities of an
acquired business (for full, partial and step acquisitions) to be recorded at
fair values, with limited exceptions.&#160;&#160;SFAS 141R requires earn-outs
and other contingent consideration to be recorded at fair value on acquisition
date and contingencies to be recorded at fair value on acquisition date with
provision for subsequent remeasurement.&#160;&#160;SFAS 141R requires
acquisitions costs to be expensed as incurred and generally requires
restructuring costs to be expensed in periods after the acquisition
date.&#160;&#160;SFAS 141R requires amounts previously called &#8220;negative
goodwill&#8221; which result from a bargain purchase in which acquisition date fair
value of identifiable net assets acquired exceeds the fair value of
consideration transferred plus any noncontrolling interest in the acquirer to be
recognized in earnings as a gain attributable to the acquirer.&#160;&#160;SFAS
141R is effective with the first annual reporting period beginning on or after
December 15, 2008.&#160;&#160;We are evaluating the impact on our financial
statements of adopting SFAS 141R.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In December, 2007, the FASB issued
Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 160 (SFAS 160), &#8220;Noncontrolling
Interests in Consolidated Financial Statements,&#8221; an amendment of ARB
51.&#160;&#160;SFAS 160 requires noncontrolling interests to be reported in the
equity section of consolidated financial statements and requires that
consolidated net income include the amounts attributable to both the parent and
the noncontrolling interests with disclosure on the face of the consolidated
income statement of net income attributable to the parent and to the
noncontrolling interests, with any losses attributable to the noncontrolling
interests in excess of the noncontrolling interests&#8217; equity to be allocated to
the noncontrolling interest.&#160;&#160;Calculation of earnings per share
amounts in the consolidated financial statements will continue to be based on
amounts attributable to the parent.&#160;&#160;SFAS 160 is effective with the
first annual reporting period beginning on or after December 15,
2008.&#160;&#160;Other than presentation differences, we do not expect SFAS160
to have a significant impact on our financial statements.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -9pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>On October 24, 2005, we entered into a
three year, $15,000,000 revolving line of credit with a maturity date of October
24, 2008 which was extended for one year to October 24, 2009.&#160;&#160;On
November 5, 2008, the line of credit was increased to $25,000,000 and extended
to November 4, 2011.&#160;&#160;Each of our wholly-owned subsidiaries has
guaranteed this credit facility, as will any future wholly-owned
subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Further, the obligation under the revolving line of
credit is secured by our pledge of our ownership in our
subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;The credit facility, which has provisions for both base
rate and LIBOR loans, is intended to provide funds for the development and
acquisition of new dialysis facilities, to meet general working capital
requirements, and for other general corporate purposes.&#160;&#160;Up to
$3,000,000 has been allocated for the repurchase of company stock should
management determine to establish a stock repurchase program, provided the
company continues to be in compliance with the financial covenants of the credit
facility after giving effect to any such stock repurchase.&#160;&#160;Borrowings
under the revolving line of credit accrue interest at the base rate for base
rate loans and the LIBOR rate for LIBOR loans plus an applicable margin, as
those terms are defined in the agreement.&#160;&#160;The LIBOR rate applicable
to a LIBOR loan is determined by the interest period selected by the company for
that particular loan, which represents the duration of the loan.&#160;&#160;We
have the right to convert a base rate loan to a LIBOR loan, and vice
versa.&#160;&#160;The agreement contains customary reporting and financial
covenant requirements for this type of credit facility.&#160;&#160;We are in
compliance with the requirements of this credit facility at December 31, 2008
and December 31, 2007.&#160;&#160;We have $13,300,000 in outstanding borrowings
under our line of credit at December 31, 2008, consisting of three LIBOR loans
with one month terms.&#160;&#160;The interest rate on the individual LIBOR loans
ranges from 3.50% to 4.9375% and includes LIBOR at issuance plus an applicable
margin of 3.0%.&#160;&#160;The individual LIBOR loans outstanding at December
31, 2008 are renewable at the end of their respective one month
terms.</font></div>

certain restrictive covenants that, among other things, limit the payment of

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">tax
positions to be taken in future returns and the amounts comprising our deferred
tax assets.&#160;&#160;The adoption of FIN 48 did not have a material impact on
our financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We file
income tax returns in the U.S. federal jurisdiction and various state and local
jurisdictions.&#160;&#160;Our federal income tax returns for 2004 through 2007
are open tax years.&#160;&#160;State and local jurisdictions that remain subject
to examination range from 2003 to 2007.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We may
from time to time be assessed interest or penalties by major tax jurisdictions,
although such assessments historically have been minimal and immaterial to our
financial results.&#160;&#160;Our policy is to recognize interest and penalties
accrued on any unrecognized tax benefits as a component of income tax
expense.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -9pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 21.6pt"></font>We have equity positions in 31
limited liability companies (&#8220;LLC&#8217;s&#8221;), and one limited partnership (&#8220;LP&#8221;) each
possessing a finite life, as well as ownership in 6 corporate
subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Based on their limited liability status, members are
not liable for the LLC&#8217;s and LP&#8217;s debts, liabilities, or
obligations.&#160;&#160;Each LLC and LP has complied with the criteria for tax
treatment as a partnership.&#160;&#160;As a result, taxable income or loss is to
be reported on each member&#8217;s respective tax returns.&#160;&#160;Income and
losses attributable to our equity position in subsidiary LLC&#8217;s and LP&#8217;s are
included in our Consolidated Statements of Income with the minority interest in
the results of operations of subsidiary LLC&#8217;s and LP&#8217;s shown separately on the
Consolidated Statements of Income.&#160;&#160;Income attributable to our equity
position in our 40% owned affiliate prior to the affiliate&#8217;s consolidation as a
subsidiary effective August 1, 2006, is shown separately on the company&#8217;s
Consolidated Statements of Income.</font></div>

stock options during 2006 resulted in a tax deduction of $84,000, corresponding
to the difference in the market value of the shares obtained on exercise and the
exercise price of the options.&#160;&#160;The reduction in income taxes payable
of approximately $31,000 resulted in a corresponding increase in additional
paid-in capital.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE
6--COMMITMENTS</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 21.6pt"></font>We have leases on facilities housing
our dialysis, administrative and medical operations, as well as equipment
leases.&#160;&#160;Total rent expense was approximately $2,676,000, $2,315,000
and $1,727,000 for the years ended December 31, 2008, 2007, and 2006,
respectively.&#160;&#160;The aggregate lease commitments at December 31, 2008

any discretionary contribution to be determined each year with only employee
contributions up to 6% of annual compensation considered when determining
employer matching.&#160;&#160;To date, employer matching expense has been
minimal.</font></div>

provide funds in excess of capital contributions subject to financing agreements
with our subsidiaries to meet working capital requirements of our dialysis
facility subsidiaries, usually until they become self-sufficient.&#160;&#160;The
operating agreements for the subsidiaries provide for cash flow and other
proceeds to first pay any such financing, exclusive of any tax payment
distributions.&#160;&#160;Minority members of the subsidiaries would be
responsible for their respective portion of the financing according to their
